situation: A React component registers a resize observer in useEffect and returns a cleanup function that calls observer.disconnect(). But the component creates a new ResizeObserver inside the effect each render while the cleanup disconnects a stale reference captured in a previous closure.
deadEnds: Added a dependency array to useEffect, but the observer was still recreated because the callback was an inline function
Tried using useRef for the observer, but forgot to update the ref before cleanup ran
Suspected the browser was ignoring disconnect(), added logging that showed disconnect was called — on the wrong instance
unlock: The cleanup function must reference the exact same object that was created during that effect invocation. Storing the observer in a local variable inside the effect (not a ref, not a state) and returning () => localObserver.disconnect() ensured the right instance was torn down.
